clue.text: Time to run demo and finish out of sequence

indicators.note: letters that are out of sequence have been jumbled from their printed order, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A instruction to rush through a demonstration and wrap it up in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two stretches of fodder: TO RUN DEMO plus FINISH supply exactly the fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, time is often described as a further dimension added to the three of space.

clue.text: Choirboy maybe briefly gets up after Fiona and Hazel

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the name's short form

parts.note: FI is a short form of the name Fiona

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters are read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano in a choir, so a choirboy is an example

explanation.surface: A boy chorister is getting up after two girls, Fiona and Hazel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like another girl's name beside Fiona, but it is the nut. 'briefly' trims TREBLE to TREBL, and 'gets up' turns that into LBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is the nut of the cultivated hazel tree, so the tree's name stands for it.

clue.text: Excessive burns doused periodically

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: An over-the-top fire put out at intervals, or burns drenched too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means going beyond what is warranted or appropriate, the sense of excessive.

clue.text: The setter's on for blocking grumpy evidence

indicators.note: blocking means the pieces sit inside the other word, obstructing it

parts.note: testy means irritable or grumpy
the setter is me, so the setter's is I'M (I am)

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be on the side of blocking some grumpy evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is a formal statement given in court, a kind of evidence.

clue.text: Fate of party, a short time after upset

indicators.note: after places the turned piece behind the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: The fate of a party, upset shortly after it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is a grim destiny or fate, often death or ruin.

clue.text: Humble state keen to be represented in pickle

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other word

parts.note: a pickle is a mess, a difficult situation

indicators.note: represented here means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A modest sort of person keen to be portrayed as in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' reads as eager, but it is only the fodder that 'to be represented' rearranges before 'in' sets it inside the pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekness is the quality of being humble and submissive, a lowly state of mind.

clue.text: Minister to fly over home counties

indicators.note: over means the word is turned back on itself, read in reverse

parts.note: to fly is to run, as in fleeing quickly
SE, south-east England, is where the Home Counties around London lie

explanation.surface: A government minister flying over the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's south-east (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to care for them, which is what ministering to them means.

clue.text: Found popular part of US to house retired soldier

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so the reversed piece goes inside

parts.note: the US is made up of states

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: Setting up a popular region of America to take in a retired soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish or set it going, which is to instigate it.

clue.text: Tell island about the missing hotel

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the island's letters are reversed

parts.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: missing means a letter is taken away from the word beside it

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Telling the story of an island without the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde; 'about' turns it to NARRA, and THE 'missing' H leaves TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or give an account.

clue.text: Most ancient item, left to the front as focus of interest

indicators.note: to the front means this letter is moved to the start of the word

parts.note: the most ancient thing is the oldest
an item is one, a single thing

explanation.surface: The oldest exhibit is placed at the front as the centrepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the front' shifts the L of OLDEST to the start, giving LODEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is a magnetic rock; figuratively, something that attracts people, a focus of attention.

clue.text: Romeo lives with woman in palace: it's a step up

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
is means exists or lives
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen who lives in the palace

explanation.surface: A man moving in with a woman who lives in a palace is going up in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The riser is the vertical part of each stair, the bit that gives the step its rise.

clue.text: It makes one sick, withdrawing article in city

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the postcode

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: withdrawing means going back, so the word's letters are reversed

parts.note: an item is an article, a thing

explanation.surface: Something nauseating about an article being pulled from a city.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London. 'withdrawing' turns ITEM to METI, which goes 'in' EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Sponsor about to secure one plant

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the numeral is held inside

parts.note: an angel is a backer or sponsor, especially of a theatre show
CA, circa, means about
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A backer is about to secure one plant, perhaps for a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic herb whose candied stems are used in cake decoration.

clue.text: Fellow rambler returning after time

indicators.note: after places the reversed word behind the letter for time
returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rover is one who roams, a rambler

explanation.surface: A walking companion coming back after some time away.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a man's name, and a fellow is any man, so the name exemplifies it.

clue.text: Freak, not counting overs in nets

parts.note: except means not counting, leaving out

indicators.note: in puts the cricket letter inside the other piece

parts.note: nets, as in takes or brings in, is read as IN
O is the cricket abbreviation for overs

explanation.surface: An unusual cricket practice where overs in the nets are not counted.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket nets are practice areas; overs are sets of six balls, abbreviated O in scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A freak is an anomaly, something that breaks the usual rule, as an exception does.

clue.text: Grow roughly fifty for the first time in grounds

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the altered grounds
fifty for the first time means the numeral replaces the first of the letters standing for time

parts.note: an estate is the grounds of a large house
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
CA, circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: Growing roughly fifty plants for the first time in the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the first' swaps the first T only, making ESLATE; 'in' then places the circa abbreviation inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to increase or intensify, the sense of grow.

clue.text: Superior fruit eaten by an android

indicators.note: eaten by means taken inside, so the pieces go within the short word

parts.note: U stands for upper class, superior
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Fine fruit being eaten by a robot.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a mechanical figure that moves by itself, like a robot or android.

clue.text: Talked of steep ditch causing furore

indicators.note: talked of signals that the word is heard spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: to steep tea is to brew it
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a boundary fence in a landscaped garden

explanation.surface: People talked of a steep ditch that caused an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for the ditch, but it is the verb, BREW. A ha-ha is a sunken ditch bounding British country-house parks.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or fuss, which is what a furore is.

clue.text: Cut police launches here

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail
the Yard, Scotland Yard, is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A police boat cut adrift at its launch.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, often just the Yard, is the headquarters of London's police.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are built and launched in a dockyard, so it is where launches happen.

clue.text: Expand day cover, avoiding November

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to envelop is to wrap or cover
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Extending insurance cover to the day, except during November.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to grow or elaborate on something, which is what expand means.

clue.text: The way papers burn

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: How you set fire to newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' sits next to 'papers' as if setting fire to them, but it is the Scottish and northern English word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Burn is a Scots word for a brook or small watercourse.

clue.text: Wed perhaps feeble, overthrown, undersized king

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dim means faint or feeble, as of a light
wee means small or undersized
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A weak, deposed, tiny king getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wed' looks like the verb marry, but it is the short form of Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Wednesday falls in the middle of the working week, so Wed is an example.

clue.text: Insubstantial odd slices of veal with holes

indicators.note: odd slices means the letters in the odd positions are taken

parts.note: porous means full of holes that let liquid through

explanation.surface: Thin, holey slices of veal that are no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaporous means like vapour, so airy, flimsy, lacking substance.

clue.text: Republican battle lacking leader that's fair

indicators.note: lacking leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a fight is a battle

explanation.surface: A Republican fight with no leader, asking whether that is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Right in the sense of just or correct means fair.

clue.text: Notice surrounding layout of hedges, staggered

indicators.note: surrounding means the first word wraps around the other

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
a maze is a puzzle of paths laid out between hedges

explanation.surface: A sign around a hedge labyrinth leaves visitors reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered here means astonished, so greatly surprised.

clue.text: Head of zoo takes age caging black animal

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word is taken
caging means enclosing, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an era is an age
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The zoo's director takes ages to cage a black animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra is a striped African animal of the horse family.

clue.text: West African nation, or part of E African one

indicators.note: part of means only a portion is kept, with letters at each end removed

parts.note: Somalia is a nation on the Horn of East Africa

explanation.surface: A geography quiz asking for a west African state or a piece of an east African one.
explanation.walkthrough: The west African nation also sits inside the east African one, with SO and A trimmed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa, capital Bamako.

clue.text: Telling stories mostly in Greek houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Tales mostly set in Greek homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' looks like an instruction to trim, but it is part of the text: mostLY IN Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is an idiom for not telling the truth, being untruthful.

clue.text: Flexible items for test carried back by porter

indicators.note: carried means held within, so the reversed pair goes inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

indicators.note: back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a bat and a pad are equipment for a cricket Test match

explanation.surface: Kit for a cricket Test carried back by a hotel porter, who must be versatile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a baggage carrier but is the beer. A Test is an international cricket match, played with bat and pads; 'back' gives DAPTAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptable means able to adjust to new conditions, so flexible.

clue.text: Dash for one, scrambling up mountain track

indicators.note: scrambling means mixing up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber making a quick dash, scrambling up a mountain path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a sprint up the track, but it is the printed line symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is one of the symbols used in writing to separate parts of a sentence, like a comma.
